Recently I had a user get hit with a newer variant of the Tesla Crypt virus which when launched, encrypts a large portion of the files on your hard drive with a randomly generated key that only they have. If you pay them money you get the key and the decryption software and can get your files back. Now for me, big fucking deal, I do snapshots nightly and incremental throughout the day and I don't need to pay anyone to get my files back. But this got me thinking about how fucking easy it is to back up these days. I mean look at the price of storage, and backup software has really come a long way, there really is no reason not to backup. Beside the obvious of don't open files from people you don't know, or visit strange websites sent in email links, etc, etc, backing up your data is the only solution besides paying the ransom, and you really shouldn't do that because it just helps to propagate the problem.

So if you don't already, I urge you to back up your data, tell your friends and family about this new virus and advise them to do the same. Maybe, just maybe, even go so far as to help them set up a solution if needed, but please for the love of all that is goatly, back up your data.

When backing up data you have to be realistic about what you want to backup. I have never had any luck trying to backup and restore a failed system or previously installed programs. Could you get it to work? on some level yes, maybe even after some testing find a solution that would work but I don't have that kind of time to worry about things that may or may not work. I backup data and that is it. If my HD dies I make sure I can access important files then just re-install and copy over the data. To backup your data you can use traditional backup software like acronis true image or you can use sync software that just syncs data between two devices. I prefer the sync option because it tends to be quicker and I can just browse the external storage to retrieve files. Options for this are goodsync, allwaysync, bittorrentsync, or you can use something like paragon backup or easus todo backup and which offers more protection. The only problem with syncing is you have to be careful how you configure it, you wouldn't want to sync and overwrite your good data with corrupted or infected data.
